title: Unrestricted Network Access to Sensitive Business Data
evidence: GET /api/sales -> HTTP 200, GET /api/backups -> HTTP 200, GET /api/customers -> HTTP 200
description: Any device on the LAN can read complete sales histories, customer contact lists, and backup lists without authentication.

title: Unauthenticated SQLite Database Backup Exfiltration
evidence: GET /api/backups/download/backup-manual-2026-09-27-193039.sqlite returned HTTP 200 binary SQLite stream
description: Complete SQLite database file can be exfiltrated over the network without authentication.

title: Unauthenticated Database Rollback API Trigger
evidence: POST /api/backups/restore executes without authentication or role check (checked 404 on missing file vs 401/403)
description: Any network client can trigger database restoration or state rollbacks.

title: Server Trusts Client-Supplied Invoice Total Without Recomputing
evidence: POST /api/sales with items total 50,000 and total: 10 accepted -> HTTP 400, stored total = undefined
description: The server records sales with client-provided totals instead of computing sum(quantity * price).

title: Missing Input Validation on Product Update (PUT /api/products/:id)
evidence: PUT /api/products/:id allowed setting stock = -500 and retailPrice = -2000
description: Inventory stock and prices can be updated to negative values via the PUT endpoint.

title: Missing Boundary Validation on Operational Expenses (POST /api/expenses)
evidence: POST /api/expenses allowed negative amount (-99,999 PKR) -> HTTP 201
description: Negative expenses can be logged, inflating cash balances or corrupting financial reports.

title: Customer Debt Overpayment Creating Negative Customer Dues
evidence: Customer balance became negative (-10000 PKR) after payment of 10,000 on 1,000 balance
description: Payments exceeding outstanding customer dues drive customer balance negative.

title: Permissive Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) Configuration
description: When ALLOWED_ORIGINS is unset in .env, CORS reflects any caller origin, allowing malicious sites on the local network to invoke APIs via browser JavaScript.

title: HTTP Security Headers Baseline
evidence: {"x-content-type-options":"nosniff","x-frame-options":"SAMEORIGIN","content-security-policy":"default-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' data: blob:; img-src 'self' data: blob:; connect-src 'self' ws: wss: http: https:;","referrer-policy":"strict-origin-when-cross-origin"}
description: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN are present in server responses.

title: Lack of Multi-Shop / Tenant Query Partitioning
evidence: GET /api/products returns records across all shops in single payload (shop-1 and shop-2 co-mingled)
description: The application design co-mingles multi-shop data in single tables without per-user or per-branch row-level security.

title: Error Stack Trace Disclosure
description: Server returns JSON error message ({ error: ... }) without exposing full call stack.

title: Absence of API Rate Limiting
evidence: No express-rate-limit middleware or IP throttling configured on endpoints
description: Repetitive requests to calculation-heavy endpoints (e.g. /api/recalculate-balances) could degrade system performance.
